papers.title: EEG Feature-level integration for robust command generation in SSVEP-based brain-computer interfaces.
papers.abstract: Steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP)-based brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have been widely studied for efficient command generation via spatiotemporal information integration and advanced stimulation paradigms. However, users may intentionally or unintentionally suppress SSVEP responses, leading to the SSVEP Blocking Response (SSVEP-BR). This phenomenon, characterized by attenuation or disappearance of SSVEP, has been largely overlooked despite its potential for command generation without additional stimuli. This study aimed to exploit SSVEP-BR to enhance command generation under limited visual stimulation. A novel detection method was proposed based on alpha rhythm sensitivity during transitions between SSVEP and SSVEP-BR states. An EEG feature-level integration strategy was further developed to integrate correlation and alpha rhythm features, enabling effective characterization of their temporal evolution. An asynchronous BCI system was implemented for real-time robotic arm control. Experiments on 11 offline subjects demonstrated that the proposed method improved SSVEP-BR detection performance. Compared with the previous SSVEP-BR detection framework, average improvements of 17.11%, 8.50%, and 5.44% were achieved in precision, recall, and specificity, respectively. Furthermore, an online robotic grasping experiment was conducted with 5 subjects, where the proposed asynchronous BCI system achieved 8-command generation using two stimulation frequencies. Unlike prior studies focusing on algorithmic optimization or stimulation design, this work introduced SSVEP-BR as an additional controllable neural response and demonstrated its effectiveness in improving command generation without increasing stimulus complexity. Incorporating SSVEP-BR into SSVEP-based BCI frameworks improved flexibility and robustness, enhancing the practicality of asynchronous brain computer interaction systems.

papers.title: Acute sleep deprivation induces ECM-associated transcription and MMP12-sensitive perivascular remodeling.
papers.abstract: Sleep deprivation (SD) disrupts brain homeostasis, but whether acute sleep loss alters extracellular matrix (ECM) programs and the structural organization of the perivascular interface remains unclear. We integrated re-analysis of three public 6-h SD transcriptomic datasets with cisterna magna tracer studies, collagen IV and hyaluronan-binding protein 2 (HABP2) imaging, cellular localization of matrix metalloproteinase-12 (MMP12), transmission electron microscopy, pharmacological MMP12 inhibition, and continuous EEG/EMG recording during ZT0-ZT6 and recovery, with manual sleep-wake scoring in 4-s epochs. Across GSE256140, GSE78215, and GSE128770, acute SD was associated with increased ECM-related transcription. In GSE256140, the most prominent differential response occurred in excitatory neurons, and six of 18 upregulated genes were annotated to the extracellular matrix term. SD increased tracer displacement relative to collagen IV, broadened collagen IV- and HABP2-positive perivascular bands, and expanded an ECM-associated perivascular compartment at the ultrastructural level. Cortical MMP12 immunoreactivity was associated most strongly with NeuN-positive structures, followed by Iba1-positive structures, with limited enrichment in GFAP-positive regions. MMP408 attenuated the SD-associated redistribution of tracer and normalized widening of the perivascular compartment, but did not significantly restore the narrowed endothelial-basement membrane complex. During ZT0-ZT6, rotating-bar SD increased wakefulness and reduced NREM and REM sleep. Recovery NREM sleep was increased in both SD groups, whereas NREM spectral profiles and relative delta power did not differ significantly among the four groups. Acute SD engages an ECM-associated transcriptional response and produces structural reorganization of the perivascular interface. The pharmacological findings identify an MMP12-sensitive component of this remodeling without establishing a single cellular source of MMP12. These results connect sleep loss to ECM and perivascular structural plasticity while separating these changes from the magnitude of early recovery sleep.

papers.title: Robust joint estimation of regional brain activity and inter-regional source covariance via full-structure covariance learning.
papers.abstract: Uncovering the mechanisms underlying cognition and brain disorders requires accurate regional source imaging and reliable characterization of inter-regional statistical dependencies. Traditional methods typically follow a two-stage pipeline that first performs source imaging and then calculates inter-regional dependence measures separately. Such a decoupled framework can propagate source-reconstruction errors to covariance-based network analyses, leading to biased source localization and distorted dependency patterns. To address these limitations, we propose a joint estimation method for regional brain source activity and source covariance via full-structure covariance learning, termed Joint Activity-Covariance Estimation via Full-Structure Covariance Learning (JAC-FS). JAC-FS constructs a Gaussian probabilistic model at the brain-region level and employs a full-structure source covariance matrix to represent regional source variance and inter-regional dependencies. In this covariance representation, diagonal entries encode marginal regional source variance, whereas off-diagonal entries quantify symmetric zero-lag covariance-based dependencies. These estimates are statistical associations and do not by themselves establish direct, directional, or causal physiological communication. A median-weighted covariance statistic suppresses high-energy artifacts, and convex surrogate optimization provides closed-form updates for source activity and source covariance. In addition, constrained noise estimation with diagonal floor protection, low-rank correlation constraints, and phased damped updates limits signal absorption and spurious covariance structure. Simulations showed that JAC-FS outperformed conventional algorithms in regional source localization, temporal recovery, source-covariance recovery against the simulated ground truth, and recovery of predefined short- and long-range covariance edges. In real MEG analyses, JAC-FS produced focal evoked source distributions and representative time courses together with evoked source-covariance patterns. These results establish JAC-FS as a unified framework for regional source imaging and zero-lag source covariance estimation.

papers.title: Reciprocal Relations Among Cognition, Insomnia, and Depression: A Cross Lagged Panel Model Among Participants of the Mexican Health and Aging Study.
papers.abstract: Understanding how insomnia symptoms, depressive symptoms, and cognitive decline are interrelated is critical for multifaceted interventions in the aging Mexican population. We examined the bidirectional associations among insomnia symptoms, depressive symptoms, and cognition in Mexican adults aged 60 and older. We used data from the Mexican Health and Aging Study (2015-2021; n=9,319). Cognition was assessed using the MHAS Cognitive Battery across three waves. Depressive and insomnia symptoms were measured at each wave using the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale and the Insomnia Severity Index, respectively. We fit random-intercept cross-lagged panel models to evaluate between- and within-person associations among these scales. Between persons, lower cognition was associated with higher depressive symptoms, and insomnia symptoms were positively associated with depression. Within persons, cognition and depressive symptoms at a prior wave predicted cognition and depressive symptoms at follow-up, respectively. Higher depressive symptoms at one wave predicted higher insomnia symptoms at the next. Insomnia symptoms at one wave were not associated with depressive symptoms or cognition at follow-up. These findings provide anunderstanding of the interrelationships ordering among insomnia, depression, and cognition, underscoring the importance of distinguishing between- and within-person associations. Interventions addressing depressive symptoms may mitigate sleep difficulties.

papers.title: Workup of Encephalopathy in Patients Receiving Cancer Immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: Cancer immunotherapy has transformed many areas of oncologic care. Neurological immune-related adverse events, particularly encephalopathy, represent potentially life-threatening complications requiring prompt recognition and intervention. Encephalopathic syndromes occur across immunotherapy modalities, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, chimeric antigen receptor-T cell therapy, and bispecific antibodies. The diagnostic challenge lies in distinguishing immune-mediated neurotoxicity from infection, metabolic derangements, disease progression, and paraneoplastic syndromes. A systematic evaluation incorporates detailed clinical assessment with neuroimaging, cerebrospinal fluid analysis, electroencephalography, and autoimmune antibody testing as appropriate. This review provides a practical approach to recognizing and assessing encephalopathy in patients receiving immunotherapy. Early multidisciplinary collaboration between neurology and oncology teams is critical for recognizing symptoms, managing adverse effects, and guiding cancer-directed treatment.

papers.title: More pronounced diurnal cortisol rhythms are longitudinally associated with less fatigue in colorectal cancer survivors: A 12-month prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Fatigue is amongst the most debilitating cancer-related symptoms, affecting up to one-third of colorectal cancer (CRC) survivors. Accumulating evidence implicates dysregulation of HPA axis as a potential mechanism contributing to chronic fatigue syndrome. We examined longitudinal associations between parameters of diurnal cortisol rhythms and fatigue in CRC survivors up to 12 months after treatment. Seventy-four survivors of CRC were assessed at 6 weeks, 6 months and 12 months after treatment. At each point, salivary samples were collected five times per day over two consecutive days to measure cortisol concentrations. Relative amplitude (RA), diurnal slope, area under the curve (AUCg) and cortisol awakening response (CAR) were derived as a comprehensive assessment of diurnal cortisol rhythms. Fatigue was assessed at all time points using the Checklist Individual Strength (CIS; range overall score: 20-140; motivational subscale: 4-28) and the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire Core 30 (EORTC; range: 0-100). Longitudinal associations were analyzed using confounder-adjusted linear mixed models, with coefficients (β) indicating differences in fatigue scores over time per SD increase in cortisol parameters. A higher RA was associated with less overall fatigue (EORTC: β= -1.42; 95%CI: -2.82, -0.03; CIS: β= -1.82; 95%CI: -3.63, -0.01). A flatter diurnal slope, indicating less decline in cortisol over the day, was associated with more fatigue (EORTC: β=1.64; 0.25, 3.03) and increased motivational fatigue (CIS: β= 0.45; 0.02, 0.88). More pronounced diurnal cortisol rhythms, specifically a higher RA and steeper diurnal slope, were longitudinally associated with less fatigue in CRC survivors. These findings may suggest that improving 24-h cortisol rhythmicity could be a target for interventions to reduce fatigue in CRC survivors, but this warrants further investigations.

papers.title: The role of comorbidities in comprehensive healthcare utilization among people with multiple sclerosis.
papers.abstract: Many people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS) live with comorbid conditions, which may contribute to more complex healthcare needs. While there have been several studies on their associations with increased hospitalizations and emergency visits, there has been limited investigation into other aspects of care (e.g., imaging) or composite indices have been used rather than individual conditions. To determine If comorbidities in PwMS are associated with utilization of a wider range of healthcare services and which specific comorbid conditions are linked to those services. Participants (n = 185) were PwMS who completed a series of questionnaires about their comorbidities and healthcare utilization over the prior 12 months as part of a larger study. Regression models were used to evaluate the relationships between healthcare utilization and specific comorbidities, controlling for age, gender, race, education, and annual income. PwMS with a comorbidity had higher utilization of several services, including more healthcare provider visits (p < 0.001), particularly with primary care (p = .041) and mental health providers (p = .003), unique providers seen (p < 0.001), active medications (p < .001), MRIs (p = .008), X-rays (p = .031), inpatient hospital stays (p = .038), and elective surgeries (p = .035). Several comorbidities, including anxiety, sleep apnea, autoimmune thyroid disease, and irritable bowel syndrome, were most frequently associated with increased service use. These findings expand upon the previous literature, demonstrating that comorbidities are associated with greater utilization of a wide range of services and the complex needs of PwMS living with multiple chronic conditions.

papers.title: Psychological resilience is associated with increased heterogeneity in the clinical aging phenotypes of patients with cancer.
papers.abstract: Cancer and its treatments are associated with accelerated aging. Emerging evidence suggests that patients' self-reports of symptoms, functional status, and resilience can identify clinical aging phenotypes. The purpose was to identify distinct clinical aging phenotypes using: six (evening fatigue, sleep disturbance, depression, state anxiety, cognitive function, physical function); seven (addition of pain); and eight (addition of resilience) clinical indicators and evaluate for differences in patient characteristics and quality of life (QOL) outcomes among the phenotypes. Outpatients (n = 1340) completed questionnaires prior to their second or third cycle of chemotherapy. Three separate latent variable models using six, seven, and eight clinical indicators were created. Differences among phenotypes in demographic and clinical characteristics and QOL outcomes were evaluated using parametric and non-parametric tests. Determination of clinically meaningful differences in QOL scores was done using Cohen's d. For the six and seven indicator models, two and three distinct phenotypes were identified, respectively. For the eight indicator model, five distinct phenotypes were identified: Very Low (32.6%), Low (32.2%), Moderate (16.4%), High (13.2%), and Very High (5.6%) clinical age. Being female, younger, having a higher comorbidity burden, and lower functional status were associated with the worst clinical aging profiles. QOL scores decreased in a stepwise fashion and differences were clinically meaningful. Inclusion of a measure of psychological resilience in the model allows for better discrimination of inter-individual variability in clinical aging phenotypes of oncology outpatients. This approach may assist with identification of patients at increased risk for accelerated aging.

papers.title: Outcomes of patients with functional/dissociative seizures after neurobehavioral therapy.
papers.abstract: Neurobehavioral therapy (NBT) is a multi-modal treatment that combines elements of interpersonal, dialectical, and cognitive behavioral therapy. This study aims to describe the efficacy and patient-centered outcomes of manualized NBT for patients with functional/dissociative seizures (FDS). We conducted a retrospective chart review of 43 patients who received NBT for FDS. Patients completed the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI), Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI), and Quality of Life in Epilepsy (QOLIE) questionnaires at the first and last sessions and a treatment outcome response grid at the final session assessing changes in social functioning, depression, anxiety, and sleep quality. FDS event frequency was ascertained at the end of treatment from self-reported seizure logs. The frequency of FDS events decreased significantly from baseline to post-treatment (p < 0.01). There was also significant improvement in BDI (p < 0.01), BAI (p = 0.01), QOL (p < 0.01), and the QOLIE seizure worry subscale (p < 0.01). The most common psychiatric comorbidities were anxiety (94.0%), depression (62.0%), and post-traumatic stress disorder (32.0%). 90.0% of patients with depression reported improvement in depression, while 73.3% of those with anxiety reported improvement in anxiety. Among those who experienced impaired social functioning as a comorbid symptom, 89.5% reported improved functioning upon completion of NBT. The results of this study suggest that manualized NBT effectively reduces seizure frequency and improves symptom comorbidities and quality of life for patients with FDS. This study supports the value of psychotherapy as a primary or adjunct treatment modality for patients with FDS.

papers.title: Wavelets and switching in bistable visual perception: Comment on "Wavelet analysis in biomedical research: A versatile tool for multiscale signal characterization and functional connectivity analysis" by Kralj et al․.
papers.abstract: This Comment highlights bistable perception as a link between wavelet-based signal characterization and functional connectivity. Prior frequency-tagged Necker-cube experiments used wavelet power to identify candidate perceptual switches and assess selective attention, while complementary EEG studies examined network organization. Integrating time-local dominance estimates with dynamic connectivity could clarify how network reconfiguration relates to switching. Such analyses require behavioral validation, consideration of wavelet resolution, and separation of connectivity from power changes. Frequency tags remain indirect perceptual markers, not intrinsic brain rhythms.

papers.title: Sleep deprivation compromises sperm quality and early embryo development by disrupting folate metabolism and DNA repair.
papers.abstract: Sleep deprivation (SD), a prevalent modern lifestyle issue, has been associated with impaired male reproductive function, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. In a mouse model, sustained SD triggered germ cell apoptosis, reduced sperm motility, and increased morphological abnormalities. Furthermore, SD compromised sperm fertilization capacity and impaired preimplantation embryo development. Proteomic analysis identified SLC46A1, a proton-coupled folate transporter, as the only consistently downregulated protein in both testicular tissue and sperm. Furthermore, the expression of methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR), a key enzyme in folate metabolism, was also markedly decreased, accompanied by reduced levels of core DNA repair proteins (RAD51 and TOPBP1). Notably, folate supplementation prior to and during SD partially restored the expression of MTHFR, RAD51, and TOPBP1, suggesting that enhanced folate availability can counteract some of the molecular alterations induced by SD. Collectively, our findings suggest a mechanistic link whereby SD disrupts folate transport and metabolism, potentially compromising DNA repair in sperm and thereby impairing sperm quality and embryonic development. This suggests that targeting folate metabolism may offer a therapeutic strategy to mitigate SD-associated male infertility.

papers.title: An integrated PCA-XGBoost method for fluorescence spectral analysis of marine microplastics.
papers.abstract: Microplastic identification based on fluorescence spectroscopy remains challenging because of spectral overlap and spectral variations associated with aging, which can affect classification performance. To address these challenges, an interpretable PCA-XGBoost framework is proposed for fluorescence spectral analysis, integrating principal component analysis (PCA) with XGBoost classification. By linking PCA loading profiles with XGBoost feature importance, the framework enables the identification of characteristic wavelengths associated with microplastic discrimination and facilitates interpretation of the spectral features underlying classification decisions. The method was evaluated using both pure and mixed microplastic samples representing multiple polymer categories under aged and unaged conditions. The proposed framework achieved an overall classification accuracy of 99.94%, while exhibiting stable feature-importance patterns across the evaluated analyses. Furthermore, the PCA-XGBoost model developed using laboratory microplastic samples was applied to real marine microplastics, demonstrating its potential for practical environmental applications.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy

papers.title: Processed electroencephalogram-guided anesthesia and its impact on postoperative delirium and perioperative efficiency: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Processed electroencephalography (pEEG) provides quantitative indices for monitoring anesthetic depth and is recommended in international guidelines. Prior meta-analyses have assessed EEG-guided anesthesia but none have evaluated available evidence stratified by pEEG technology. We performed a systematic literature review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials in adults undergoing surgical, endoscopic, or dental procedures comparing pEEG-guided with non-pEEG-guided anesthesia. Primary outcomes were anesthetic drug use (TIVA and volatile agents) and postoperative delirium (POD ≤10 days). Secondary outcomes were extubation time, wake-up time, time to orientation, and post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) length of stay. Searches (PubMed Central, MEDLINE) were conducted on 11 April 2025; the protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251067170). Random-effects models produced standardized mean differences (SMD), mean differences (MD), and risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence interval (CI). Eighty-seven RCTs (30,611 patients; 13,586 pEEG; 17,025 non-pEEG) were included. pEEG significantly reduced propofol use (SMD -0.42, 95% CI -0.74 to -0.10; p = 0.01) and volatile anesthetic use (SMD -1.27, 95% CI -1.88 to -0.66; p < 0.01). The risk of POD decreased by 27% (RR 0.73, 95% CI 0.63 to 0.84; p < 0.01). Efficiency outcomes favored pEEG: extubation time (MD -2.90 min, 95% CI -3.64 to -2.16; p < 0.01), wake-up time (MD -1.83 min, 95% CI -2.42 to -1.25; p < 0.01), time to orientation (MD -4.11 min, 95% CI -6.99 to -1.23; p < 0.01), and PACU length of stay (MD -2.81 min, 95% CI -4.66 to -0.96; p < 0.01). Subgroup analyses suggested benefits were most consistently observed for BIS; estimates for Entropy and SEDLine were less precise due to fewer studies. Heterogeneity was substantial for several outcomes. Across 87 RCTs, pEEG-guided monitoring utilizing multiple device types improved perioperative efficiency and reduced POD compared with not using pEEG. Evidence is strongest for BIS; further well-reported trials are needed to delineate device-specific effects.

papers.title: Concordance between magnetoencephalography and intracranial EEG and association with surgical outcomes in MRI-negative epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Magnetoencephalography (MEG) is increasingly used in the presurgical evaluation of drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE), particularly in MRI-negative cases. However, the relationship between MEG localization, intracranial EEG (iEEG) concordance, underlying pathology, and surgical outcomes remains incompletely defined. We performed a retrospective cohort study of 51 patients with MRI-negative DRE who underwent MEG and iEEG evaluation at our center from 2009 to 2025. MEG spike source localization was categorized as complete, partial, or discordant relative to the iEEG-defined SOZ using a lobar-level concordance framework. Surgical outcomes were assessed in 29 patients who underwent resective surgery using the Engel classification at 6 months, 1 year, 2 years, and last follow-up. Associations between concordance, pathology, and outcomes were evaluated using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests as appropriate, with Monte-Carlo exact inference used for sparse contingency tables. MEG identified localizing interictal abnormalities in 33 of 51 patients (65%), while 18 (35%) had no MEG spikes. Among 32 patients with both localizing MEG and an iEEG-defined SOZ, complete lobar-level concordance was observed in 23 (72%), partial concordance in 7 (22%), and discordance in 2 (6%). At 1 year after resection, Engel class I outcomes were observed in 10 of 11 patients (91%) with complete concordance, 5 of 5 (100%) with partial concordance, and 5 of 8 patients (63%) with MEG-negative studies. Exploratory Monte-Carlo exact analysis demonstrated a significant impact of histopathology on the distribution of MEG-iEEG concordance (p = 0.004). Histopathology was not a significant predictor of study MEG positivity. MEG identified localizing interictal abnormalities in approximately two-thirds of this selected cohort of patients with MRI-negative DRE. When MEG was localizing and an iEEG-defined SOZ was identified, lobar-level concordance was common. Because MEG could inform invasive evaluation, these findings reflect concordance within an MEG-informed clinical workflow rather than independent validation against iEEG. Surgical outcome and histopathology associations were exploratory and will need to be validated in larger cohorts.

papers.title: Autonomy satisfaction and bedtime procrastination among generation Z university students: The serial mediating roles of general self-efficacy and AI dependence.
papers.abstract: With the rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into higher education, university students' daily behaviors are increasingly shaped by technology use. Bedtime procrastination has emerged as a common self-regulation problem among Generation Z students. However, the psychological mechanisms linking environmental resources and technology-related behaviors to sleep outcomes remain insufficiently understood. This study examined the associations between autonomy satisfaction and bedtime procrastination and the mediating roles of general self-efficacy and AI dependence. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 717 Chinese university students using cluster sampling. Standardized self-report measures assessed autonomy satisfaction, general self-efficacy, AI dependence, and bedtime procrastination. Data were analyzed using SPSS 26.0 and Mplus 8.0. Structural equation modeling and bias-corrected bootstrap (5000 resamples) were employed to test direct and indirect effects. Autonomy satisfaction was positively associated with general self-efficacy and negatively associated with AI dependence and bedtime procrastination. General self-efficacy was negatively associated with both AI dependence and bedtime procrastination, while AI dependence was positively associated with bedtime procrastination. Mediation analysis revealed that both general self-efficacy and AI dependence served as significant mediators, with AI dependence accounting for a larger proportion of the indirect effect. A significant serial mediation pathway was also observed. The findings suggest that autonomy satisfaction was associated with bedtime procrastination through both cognitive and behavioral mechanisms. AI dependence plays a particularly important role as a proximal behavioral pathway. These results highlight the need to promote balanced AI use and strengthen students' self-regulation in technology-rich learning environments.

papers.title: The mediating role of perceived social support in the relationship between perceived stress and sleep disorders in mothers of children with food allergies.
papers.abstract: This study was conducted to examine the mediating role of perceived social support in the relationship between perceived stress and sleep disturbances in mothers of children with food allergies. This study was conducted as a descriptive-cross-sectional study. "DASS-21 Scale," "Basic Scale of Insomnia Complaints and Sleep Quality," and "Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support" were used to collect the research data. The study included 89 mothers. A Structural Equation Model (SEM) was established, and the mediating model was analyzed by using the PROCESS macro (Model 3). The results demonstrated that maternal perceived stress significantly and negatively predicted perceived social support scores (β = -0.258, p = 0.012), while it positively predicted insomnia complaints and significantly worsened sleep quality (β = 0.813, p < 0.001). It was found that mothers' perceived levels of social support negatively predicted insomnia and sleep quality (β1 = -0.205; p < 0.001). According to the results of the model, mothers' perceived social support scores explained 36.6% of the variance in their stress scores (R2 = 0.366). It was found that social support plays a mediating role in the relationship between the stress perceived by mothers and insomnia and sleep quality. During routine clinical check-ups for children diagnosed with food allergies, not only the child's physical health but also the mother's psychological state should be assessed. Considering that perceived stress in mothers directly and strongly affects sleep quality, pediatric nurses and physicians should be encouraged to use brief stress and sleep screening tools.

papers.title: Domiciliary sleep assessment technology for obstructive sleep apnoea diagnosis and upper airway surgical management - A scoping review.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) is characterised by episodic complete or partial upper airway collapse during sleep. Diagnostic methods such as polysomnography (PSG) are resource-intensive and of limited utility for characterising upper-airway collapse to guide surgery. The expanding use of domiciliary sleep assessments presents an opportunity to improve access to OSA diagnosis. This review aims to evaluate the accuracy, clinical utility and limitations of domiciliary sleep assessment to diagnose OSA and localise airway collapse. A scoping review was performed using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library. Articles published between January 1, 2015, and September 1, 2025, were included. The analysis focused on diagnostic performance compared with PSG, with exploratory airway phenotyping. Thirty-three studies met inclusion criteria. Domiciliary sleep assessment showed a sensitivity and specificity for moderate-to-severe OSA exceeding 90% in several studies of selected high pre-test probability cohorts. However, performance to detect mild OSA remains suboptimal. In contrast, entropy-based audio analysis and mandibular positioners show promise in obstructive site localisation and treatment selection. Domiciliary sleep assessments are limited by night-to-night variability and inadequate airway flow phenotyping. Domiciliary sleep assessment has clinically useful accuracy to diagnose moderate-to-severe OSA. Enhanced integration of upper airway flow characteristics represents a key area of development, with the potential to improve patient selection for targeted surgical interventions.

papers.title: Predictive value of EEG/ECG biomarkers for treatment response in depression.
papers.abstract: Major depressive episodes frequently show limited response to first-line treatments, motivating the search for objective biomarkers. EEG/ECG-based support tools aggregating electrophysiological predictors may guide treatment selection. We examined whether antidepressant treatments concordant with an EEG/ECG-biomarker report were associated with higher response rates. We retrospectively analyzed adults with ICD-10 depressive disorder or bipolar depression treated with electroconvulsive therapy (ECT), repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), (es)ketamine, or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) between 2022 and 2024. Resting-state EEG with simultaneous ECG generated individualized biomarker reports with modality-specific response likelihoods. Treatment chosen by clinical teams was classified as concordant or non-concordant; response was derived from routinely collected clinical scales. Among 153 patients (ECT n = 53, rTMS n = 48, (es)ketamine n = 36, SSRIs n = 16), response rates were higher for concordant vs non-concordant treatments: ECT 70% vs 50%, rTMS 30% vs 13%, (es)ketamine 31% vs 10%, and SSRIs 100% vs 11%. Overall, 46% (42/92) of concordant vs. 26% (14/54) of non-concordant patients responded (absolute difference + 20 percentage points; relative increase ≈77%; number needed to treat ≈5). Concordance with EEG/ECG biomarkers correlated with higher treatment response, warranting confirmation in prospective trials. EEG/ECG-based decision support may enhance antidepressant treatment response in everyday clinical practice.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology

papers.title: Early Characterization of Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy: Contribution of Biochemical, Imaging, and Electrophysiological Markers to Patient Profiling in the Ancillary Cohort LyTONEPAL.
papers.abstract: To identify and characterize different profiles of newborns with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) according to clinical, biochemical, electrophysiological, and brain imaging data. An analysis was conducted on the Long-Term Outcome of Neonatal hypoxic EncePhALopathy in the era of neuroprotective treatment with hypothermia ancillary cohort, including 204 newborns with mild to severe HIE. Multiple factor analysis and hierarchical ascendant classification were performed using clinical, biochemical, electrophysiological, and imaging data to establish clusters representing the cohort. The combination of electrophysiological, biochemical, and imaging data provided the best representation of the ancillary cohort, accounting for 36.5% of the explained variance. Two clusters of patients were identified using these factors. Patients allocated to cluster 2 were more likely to present severe HIE (70.8%; P < 0.001), severe electroencephalograph patterns (65.2%; P < 0.001), brain injuries (66.3%; P < 0.001) and biochemical abnormalities in pH (6.91 ± 0.18; P < 0.05), lactate levels (14.7 ± 5.5; P < 0.001), and glycemia (P < 0.05). By contrast, cluster 1 was predominantly represented by neonates with mild HIE symptoms, better electroencephalograph patterns, biochemical markers, and no brain lesions. There were no significant differences in maternal and obstetrical data, particularly sentinel events, between the clusters. Early consideration of the association of biochemical, electrophysiological, and brain imaging data in neonates with HIE would allow a better and more precise characterization of the HIE profile of the newborn and its severity, compared to the sole clinical evaluation through Sarnat or Thompson score in this population.

papers.title: Early movement intention recognition via corticomuscular synchrony in complex tasks.
papers.abstract: Intuitive control of assistive robots requires precise decoding of movement intention before muscle activation. While corticomuscular coherence (CMC) tracks descending corticospinal drive, decoding pre-onset intention during complex, multi-target tasks remains challenging. This study identifies stable CMC markers characterizing the transition from motor planning to execution. Twelve healthy volunteers performed target-directed reaching tasks using a 6-DoF robotic arm controlled via a wireless wearable inertial interface. The experimental protocol evaluated two distinct conditions: a four-target reaching task arranged in a semi-circle and a more complex two-target reaching task with 3D obstacles requiring trajectory planning. An exploratory analysis was performed using wavelet transform coherence (WCT) to map the pre-movement time-frequency dynamics and simulated real-time framework was subsequently implemented to classify 'rest' and 'intention' states, comparing CMC metrics against EEG power spectral density (PSD). Exploratory time-frequency analysis using WCT revealed a statistically significant pre-motor desynchronization across the high theta, alpha, and beta bands, which was concentrated predominantly 100 to 200 ms prior to EMG activation. In the classification framework, the metric leveraging phase dynamics in CMC outperformed the PSD classifiers, achieving a mean accuracy of 0.80 accross participants and highest peak of intention classification around 100 ms before EMG onset. Corticomuscular coherence provides a highly reliable and very early neurophysiological marker of higher-order motor planning and sensorimotor integration before physical execution. Integrating these phase-desynchronization features into future real-time multi-sensor fusion architectures offers a viable strategy to enhance intent recognition accuracy and shorten system latencies in assistive rehabilitation.

papers.title: Family-Supported mHealth Coaching for Middle-Aged Men With Chronic Liver Disease and Metabolic Risk Factors: Protocol for a Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Chronic liver disease (CLD) remains a substantial public health burden, particularly among middle-aged men with metabolic risk factors. Sustained lifestyle modification is essential for preventing disease progression, but long-term self-management in this population is often suboptimal. Although mobile health (mHealth) interventions may support self-management, most are patient-centered and rarely incorporate structured family participation. This study aims to develop a family-supported mHealth coaching intervention for middle-aged men with CLD and metabolic risk factors, evaluate the feasibility of the intervention and trial procedures, and explore preliminary app usability and changes in patient- and family-related outcomes through a pilot randomized controlled trial (RCT). This 2-arm, parallel-group pilot RCT was conducted at the Liver Center of Severance Hospital, Yonsei University Health System, Seoul, Republic of Korea. Eligible patients were male outpatients aged 40 to 64 years who had CLD for at least 6 months and at least 1 metabolic risk factor. The planned sample size was 82 patients, with 41 patients per group. Enrolled patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to a 12-week family-supported mHealth coaching intervention or usual outpatient care plus a standardized educational video delivered via text message. Guided by the information-motivation-behavioral skills (IMB) model, the intervention integrates app-based self-monitoring, individualized feedback, online coaching, and opportunities for family participation. The feasibility and acceptability of the intervention and trial procedures will be evaluated. Primary outcomes are self-management behavior, perceived social support, depressive symptoms, and sleep quality; secondary outcomes include physical and clinical indicators and family experiences. Outcomes were assessed at baseline (week 0) and postintervention (week 12). Between-group changes will be examined using appropriate parametric or nonparametric tests, with an analysis of covariance used for baseline-adjusted comparisons. Effect estimates will be reported with 95% CIs and interpreted as preliminary. Complete-case analyses will be conducted without imputation of missing data. This study was funded in March 2023 and received institutional review board approval on April 9, 2025 (approval 4-2025-0117). The first participant was enrolled in May 2025, and data collection was completed in March 2026. A total of 52 patient participants were enrolled and randomized, of whom 35 completed the 12-week follow-up, corresponding to an overall attrition rate of 32.7%. Data analysis and preparation of the main trial manuscript are currently underway, with submission for publication anticipated in winter 2026. This pilot RCT evaluates an IMB model-informed, family-supported mHealth coaching intervention integrating app-based self-monitoring and individualized coaching. The findings will provide preliminary evidence regarding feasibility, acceptability, and changes in patient- and family-related outcomes and will inform intervention refinement and the design of a future definitive RCT. Clinical Research Information Service KCT0010494; https://tinyurl.com/75m6c7c6. DERR1-10.2196/95490.

papers.title: An Exceptional Mobility Group Among Older Adults: Protocol for the Super Movers Study.
papers.abstract: Gait dysfunction is a preclinical marker of Alzheimer disease (AD) and related dementias (ADRD), often emerging years before clinical diagnosis. While much of the existing literature has focused on the pathological mechanisms driving motor and cognitive decline, the neural and biological substrates that confer resilience against such decline remain poorly understood. Individuals who maintain exceptional gait performance into advanced age, termed Super Movers, represent a unique phenotype of resilient aging. Understanding the biological profile of these individuals offers a unique and largely untapped window into the mechanisms underlying healthy aging and resilience to dementia. This study aims to identify the structural, functional, neurophysiological, and molecular brain characteristics that distinguish older adults with exceptional mobility from their usual and slow-moving peers, and to determine whether these characteristics predict cognitive and physical decline over time. We hypothesize that the interplay between protective and pathological mechanisms in aging gives rise to structural, functional, neurophysiological, and molecular brain changes that manifest along a continuum from resilient gait to gait dysfunction. We aim to enroll 350 adults aged 65 years and older from community and clinic settings. Participants will be classified by gait speed into fast, usual, and slow movers using age- and sex-specific thresholds; fast movers aged 80 years and older will be designated as Super Movers. All participants will undergo comprehensive assessments at baseline, including brain imaging, mobile electroencephalogram (EEG) recorded during walking, multisensory integration (MSI), comprehensive blood profiling, blood-based markers of neurodegeneration, epigenetic and proteomic aging clocks, and detailed cognitive testing. Follow-up assessments will be conducted annually in person and every 6 months by telephone. This study was funded by the National Institute on Aging (R01AG089096; PI: Joe Verghese) and has received Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval from Stony Brook University. Enrollment is currently underway. Fast and Super Movers are expected to demonstrate distinct neural substrates, EEG activation signatures, and favorable biomarker profiles relative to usual and slow movers. By shifting the scientific focus from the biology of gait decline toward the biology of gait resilience, this protocol is uniquely positioned to advance our understanding of healthy aging and inform novel strategies for dementia prevention.

papers.title: Monolithic and scalable capacitive electrodes leveraging parasitic capacitance for full-body pressure mapping.
papers.abstract: Scaling capacitive pressure sensor arrays to large areas remains challenging due to electrode alignment errors, fabrication complexity, and limited dynamic range inherent in conventional parallel-plate architectures. Here, we present a scalable capacitive pressure sensor array based on a monolithic electrode architecture, where transmitter and receiver electrodes are co-integrated into a single substrate. A deformable dielectric and a floating ground (GND) layer are positioned above, eliminating alignment errors and reducing the layer-stacking process by 20%. The parasitic capacitance between the electrodes and GND layer is intentionally incorporated into the sensing mechanism, enabling stable pressure detection with effective electromagnetic interference shielding. The resulting 2911-cell array (1.7 m by 1.0 m) achieves 30 Hz full-body pressure mapping with high linearity (R2 = 0.994). Demonstrations in sleep posture classification, pressure injury prevention, and exercise monitoring validate the platform's versatility for healthcare and human-machine interfaces.

papers.title: A self-supervised reconstruction framework for segment-level detection of task-induced deviations in multi-channel EEG.
papers.abstract: Understanding brain activations during mental arithmetic tasks provides valuable insights into cognitive processing. However, analyses of the same electroencephalogram (EEG) dataset have produced inconsistent findings about the cortical regions involved, raising methodological questions about global signal treatment. Detecting task-related activations without pre-labelled datasets further remains challenging when supervised approaches are not applicable. This study presents a self-supervised framework for segment-based anomaly detection using deep learning to identify EEG signal outliers during mental arithmetic. Using a hierarchical variational auto-encoder, the study reconstructed multichannel EEG data segmented into 1-second intervals and trained exclusively on resting-state recordings. The study assessed reconstruction quality using multiple error metrics, including dynamic time warping, short-time Fourier transform loss, and signal-to-noise ratio, applied individually to channel segments. Outlier segments were detected based on the elevated reconstruction error relative to the resting baseline, using an unsupervised detection method. By analysing deviations at the segment level rather than treating the signal globally, the proposed framework captured transient cortical dynamics that may otherwise be obscured. The results demonstrated that these outlier segments exhibited distinct temporal and spectral characteristics, particularly within the delta, theta, and beta bands, and were most frequently located in peripheral electrodes such as Fp2, O1, O2, P3, and T6. Additionally, co-occurrence analysis uncovered functional patterns of simultaneous anomalies across specific electrode pairs and triplets, suggesting temporally dynamic and spatially distributed cognitive processes during arithmetic reasoning. Overall, the proposed framework provided a fine-grained temporal and spatial characterisation of EEG deviations during mental arithmetic and offers a methodological perspective that helped explain discrepancies in previously reported electrode-level findings.

papers.title: Effects of a sleep program on sleep, performance and health in university students: Study protocol for a randomised controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Insomnia and poor sleep are highly prevalent among university students and are linked to impaired mental and physical health, reduced cognitive functioning, and lower academic performance. Existing interventions for insomnia include cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBT-I), mindfulness, and sleep hygiene. CBT-I is widely recognised as effective but remains difficult to access for the general population and lack scalability, long-term follow-up, and feasibility in non-clinical settings. Pragmatic, group-based approaches that can be delivered within the university and are tailored to help students develop self-endorsed routines and competencies for better sleep, creating sustainable changes that extend beyond the program period, is needed. This study is a pragmatic, two-arm randomised controlled trial evaluating the effectiveness of a group-based sleep program for university students with insomnia symptoms. A total of 118 full-time students aged 18-30 meeting diagnostic criteria for chronic insomnia disorder will be randomized (1:1) to either the intervention or a wait-list control group. The intervention comprises 12 weekly 90-minute group sessions followed by nine monthly follow-up meetings, facilitated by trained coaches. The program integrates core elements of CBT-I with motivational and coping strategies, delivered in an interactive and peer-supported format. The primary outcome is change in insomnia severity measured by the Bergen Insomnia Scale. Secondary outcomes include subjective and objective sleep measures, mental health, cognitive performance, academic attainment, health behaviours, physical fitness, and biological markers. Assessments will be conducted at baseline, post-program (12 weeks), and 12 months. A mixed methods process evaluation will assess fidelity, acceptability, mechanisms of impact, and contextual influences. This trial will be among the first pragmatic evaluations of a structured, group-based sleep intervention tailored to university students with insomnia. Key strengths include the randomised controlled design, comprehensive outcome assessment, 12-month follow-up, and embedded process evaluation. If effective, the program could provide a feasible, scalable, and cost-effective model to improve sleep and therein health, and academic performance in young adults in higher education.

papers.title: Multidomain Outcomes of a Digital Self-Management Program in Rural Adults With Chronic Conditions: Single-Arm Prospective Interventional Study.
papers.abstract: Chronic disease and comorbid mental health problems disproportionately affect rural and underserved populations. Digital self-management programs are potentially scalable, but evaluations often focus on narrow outcomes. This study examined 12-month longitudinal changes in psychological and multidomain outcomes among Pictou County Patient Empowerment Program participants and explored co-occurring changes and psychological moderators. This single-arm prospective interventional study enrolled 182 community-dwelling adults with ≥1 chronic condition in Pictou County, Nova Scotia, between October 2023 and August 2025 through community-based outreach. Median age was 60 (IQR 51-68) years, 155 of 182 (85.2%) participants were women, and the median number of chronic conditions was 3 (IQR 1-3). The initial 6-month digital intervention delivered brief daily modules targeting physical activity, nutrition, stress regulation, sleep, habit formation, and social connection, followed by a 6-month lower-intensity maintenance period during which monthly group videoconference sessions continued to be offered. Outcomes were assessed at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months. Primary outcomes were illness perceptions (Brief Illness Perception Questionnaire), perceived stress (10-item Perceived Stress Scale [PSS-10]), disease-related worry (10-item Questionnaire on Distress in Cancer Patients), life satisfaction (Satisfaction With Life Scale), and mental well-being (World Health Organization-Five Well-Being Index [WHO-5]). Secondary outcomes assessed the physical, behavioral, and psychosocial domains. Generalized estimating equations estimated population-averaged longitudinal changes, adjusted for age, sex, relationship status, comorbidity burden, and baseline depression or anxiety medication use. Exploratory models examined co-occurring changes and moderation. Tests were 2-sided with α=.05. Across outcomes and follow-up assessments, completion ranged from 58.2% (95% CI 51.0%-65.2%; 106/182) to 65.4% (95% CI 58.2%-71.9%; 119/182). At 12 months, illness perceptions decreased (β=-7.3, 95% CI -9.7 to -4.9), perceived stress decreased (β=-2.4, 95% CI -3.5 to -1.3), disease-related worry decreased (β=-6.3, 95% CI -7.8 to -4.7), life satisfaction increased (β=2.5, 95% CI 1.4-3.5), and mental well-being increased (β=10.4, 95% CI 7.2-13.5; all P<.001). Secondary outcomes improved across fatigue, sleep, diet quality, sedentary behavior, spiritual well-being, mental health-related quality of life, weight, and BMI. Exploratory analyses showed that improvements in fatigue, sleep quality, and illness perceptions co-occurred with greater well-being and life satisfaction and lower perceived stress and disease-related worry at both follow-up assessment points. Clinically meaningful stress improvement (≥4-point PSS-10 reduction) was achieved by 36.4% (95% CI 27.3%-45.6%, 39/107) and 43.4% (95% CI 34.0%-52.8%, 46/106) participants at 6 and 12 months, respectively. At 12 months, 43.5% (95% CI 34.2%-52.9%, 47/108) participants reported clinically meaningful improvement in mental well-being (≥10-point WHO-5 increase). Participation in this low-bandwidth, home-based digital self-management program was associated with sustained psychological, physical, and behavioral improvements among rural adults with chronic conditions. These multidomain findings support randomized controlled evaluation of scalable digital self-management approaches as adjuncts to rural chronic disease care.

papers.title: Capturing Class Differences in EEG Connectivity with Class-discriminative Multivariate IMagInary Coherency (CMIMIC).
papers.abstract: A major challenge in EEG/MEG analysis is to characterize task-dependent functional connectivity in a way that is statistically robust and spatially interpretable, without prior source modeling or region-of-interest selection. Comparing connectivity between conditions is statistically demanding due to the high dimensionality of connectivity estimates, and spatial interpretability is compromised when effects are fragmented across many tests. Here, we introduce Class-discriminative Multivariate ImagInary Coherency (CMIMIC), a multivariate method that maximizes differences in the imaginary part of coherency between two classes, enabling the robust identification of condition-specific functional interactions while minimizing spurious connectivity due to volume conduction. We evaluated CMIMIC using simulations and resting-state EEG data of young and older adults in eyes open and eyes closed conditions. In simulations, CMIMIC recovered both the temporal dependencies between sources and their underlying generating networks. On empirical data, the CMIMIC-based pipeline consistently outperformed those based on traditional imaginary coherence (ImCoh) across classifiers and conditions. All methods performed better with eyes open than closed, but CMIMIC showed only a modest performance drop, in contrast to substantial losses for ImCoh. Feature stability analyses revealed that CMIMIC identifies a core set of informative sources largely shared across conditions, whereas ImCoh features were more condition-specific. CMIMIC also provides spatially interpretable source configurations that align well with known neurophysiological effects, offering a reliable, interpretable, and condition-robust approach for extracting discriminative connectivity features from EEG data.

papers.title: Electroencephalography Alpha-Band Oscillations as Potential Indicators of Executive Subcomponents Dysfunction correlating to the Severity of Cerebral Small Vessel Disease.
papers.abstract: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) relates to executive dysfunction. While electroencephalography (EEG) alpha-band oscillations are promising biomarkers for cognitive impairment, their relationship with specific subcomponents of executive function in CSVD remains unclear. We aimed to investigate the association between EEG alpha-band oscillations and subcomponents of executive function-inhibitory control and working memory-among patients with CSVD. This was a cross-sectional analysis of an ongoing national registry research of CSVD (KY 2019-140-01). Five-minute resting-state EEG was recorded for analyzing occipital and frontal alpha-band indexes including peak frequency (PFα), occipital-frontal ΔPFα, and neurophysiological cognitive level. Inhibitory control and working memory were respectively evaluated by the Victoria Stroop Test (VST) and Digit Span. Associations and screening performance were assessed through logistic regression and ROC-AUC analysis with bootstrap internal validation. A total of 181 CSVD patients (age=60±12.0 years, male=61.9%) were recruited. After adjusting for age, gender, education, and CSVD severity, all PFα were associated with VST trial-2 completion time and VST composite time, respectively (all p<0.05). PFα(O1) have shown association with VST trial-3 completion time (p<0.05). PFα(O1) and PFα(O2) were associated with the high interference score, respectively (all p<0.05). We have set up fifty-six alpha-band-related models, and twenty-four models were selected with apparent AUC ranging from 0.6 to 0.83. The highest apparent AUC for inhibitory control impairment was 0.83, with an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.80. Alpha-band oscillations showed no robust association with working memory. In conclusion, resting-state EEG alpha-band parameters were associated with inhibitory control, but had no connection with working memory, in patients with CSVD. These findings suggested that resting-state EEG alpha-band oscillations can serve as an objective, accessible tool for assessing specific executive deficits in patients with CSVD.

papers.title: Health behavior concordance in middle-aged and older Chinese couples: longitudinal analysis from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS).
papers.abstract: Spousal concordance in health has implications for couple-based interventions, yet evidence on health behavior concordance in couples has been limited. This study examined cross-sectional and longitudinal spousal associations for seven health behaviors among middle-aged and older Chinese couples. Data came from 6,579 couples (13,158 individuals) in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS, 2011-2018). Behaviors included obesity, physical inactivity, social inactivity, short/long sleep, extended napping, current smoking, and heavy drinking. Generalized estimating equations (GEE) was used to estimate cross-sectional spousal associations. Cross-lagged panel models (CLPM) tested longitudinal directional influences, and joint Wald tests assessed whether directional effects differed significantly by sex. Significant cross-sectional spousal associations emerged for all seven health behaviors. Longitudinally, bidirectional spousal influence was observed for short/long sleep (wife-to-husband OR=1.17; husband-to-wife OR=1.19), heavy drinking (wife-to-husband OR=2.78; husband-to-wife OR=2.29), social inactivity (wife-to-husband OR=1.14; husband-to-wife OR=1.11), and extended napping (wife-to-husband OR=1.55; husband-to-wife OR=1.28). Obesity showed a significant husband-to-wife path (OR=1.30). Physical inactivity and smoking showed no significant longitudinal influence in either direction. Formal testing found no statistically significant difference in magnitude between wife-to-husband and husband-to-wife paths for any behavior. Spousal concordance was moderate to strong for health behaviors, and longitudinal analyses revealed genuinely bidirectional mutual influence. These findings suggest that couple-based behavioral change interventions may be more effective than individual-focused approaches to benefit both members in the couple.

papers.title: Workplace noise exposure and sleep among small-scale industrial metal workers in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the relationship between workplace noise exposure and sleep outcomes among high noise exposed small-scale industrial metal workers and a low noise exposed control group in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. A cross-sectional design was employed, where 66 metal workers from small-scale metal industries in informal sectors (high noise exposed) and 22 cleaners from university teaching hospital in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania (low noise exposed) were included. Noise levels were assed using personal noise dosimeters (Brüel and Kjær type 4448), while sleep parameters were measured using ActiWatch devices. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 27. The average 8-h noise exposure level (LAeq,8 h) among the high noise exposed workers was 97.9 ± 5.5 dBA, compared to 76.6 ± 3.3 dBA among the low noise exposed workers. Sleep efficiency averaged 80.4 ± 7.7% and 74.7 ± 11.7%, and average sleep duration was 454.4 ± 93.3 min and 360.7 ± 90.0 min in high noise exposed workers and low noise exposed workers, respectively. There was a statistically significant difference among the two groups in terms of sleep duration (p = 0.001) and sleep efficiency (p = 0.023), when adjusting for age and education. No statistically significant differences were found in sleep onset latency and wake after sleep onset when comparing the two groups. Workers exposed to high daytime noise levels demonstrated longer sleep duration and better sleep efficiency compared to workers exposed to low noise levels. Further longitudinal studies with larger sample sizes and extended monitoring periods are needed to confirm the findings.

papers.title: Hypothalamic hamartoma in a child with Pallister-Hall syndrome: Report of a rare lesion successfully managed with multidisciplinary approach.
papers.abstract: Hypothalamic hamartomas (HH) are rare, benign malformations of the hypothalamus, often presenting with gelastic seizures, developmental delays, and endocrine abnormalities. These lesions can disrupt normal hypothalamic function, resulting in gelastic seizures, endocrine abnormalities, and neurocognitive or behavioral disturbances. HHs may be associated with syndromic conditions like Pallister-Hall syndrome. We report the case of a 2-year-old female with gelastic seizures, syndactyly, polydactyly, and urogenital anomalies, suggestive of Pallister-Hall syndrome. The electroencephalogram was normal, and magnetic resonance imaging of the brain showed a well-defined, mildly T2 hyperintense, T1 isointense, non-enhancing lesion in the suprasellar region. The patient underwent subtotal resection and disconnection of the hypothalamic mass, which was histopathologically confirmed as HH. Postoperatively, she developed transient diabetes insipidus (DI), followed by syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion (SIADH), both of which resolved with appropriate management. This case underscores the importance of recognizing HH as a rare but distinct lesion with characteristic clinical and radiologic features. Early diagnosis is crucial for appropriate management and for preventing long-term neuroendocrine and behavioural complications. A multidisciplinary approach is essential for diagnosing and managing HH, especially when associated with syndromic features. This case adds to the existing literature by highlighting the surgical and endocrine management challenges in syndromic HH.

papers.title: Outcome-Blind EEG Microstate Topography After Cardiac Arrest: Spatial Expression of a Lateralized Microstate and Association with Neurological Outcome.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is central to neurological assessment after cardiac arrest, yet conventional approaches predominantly characterize amplitude, frequency content, continuity, suppression, reactivity, or predefined pathological patterns. EEG microstates provide a complementary framework by describing quasi-stable configurations of the global scalp electric field. We investigated whether an outcome-blind microstate decomposition of EEG from comatose survivors of cardiac arrest identifies reproducible spatial states associated with neurological outcome. We performed a secondary analysis of the multicenter I-CARE/PhysioNet database. Following prespecified EEG screening requiring continuous 19-channel recordings of at least 300 s, 567 subjects were included (34 excluded at preflight). Microstate reconstruction was performed outcome-blind using a fixed 300-s continuous baseline analysis window, GFP-peak sampling capped at 500 peaks per patient, and polarity-invariant clustering across K = 2-10. After model-order evaluation, the K = 4 solution was frozen and backfitted at the patient level. Associations between microstate metrics and neurological outcome were evaluated using unadjusted, multivariable, dose-response, ROC discrimination, and extensive resampling analyses. The primary outcome analysis included 567 patients: 209 with favorable (CPC 1-2) and 358 with unfavorable (CPC 3-5) neurological outcomes. M2 global explained variance (GEV) was higher in patients with favorable outcome (median 0.0852 vs. 0.0564; rank-biserial correlation = 0.185; p = 0.000243; false-discovery-rate [FDR]-adjusted p = 0.000568 within the four-state GEV family). M2 GEV was inversely associated with CPC severity (Spearman rho = -0.144; p = 0.000583; FDR-adjusted p = 0.001419). Standalone ROC analysis yielded an AUC of 0.59 (95% CI 0.54-0.64). After adjustment for age, sex, and shockable rhythm in the extended cohort without return-of-spontaneous-circulation (ROSC) time (N = 535), each 1-SD increase in M2 GEV was associated with greater odds of favorable outcome (OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.07-1.58; p = 0.0092). In the complete-case model additionally adjusted for ROSC time (N = 292), the association remained significant (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.10-1.97; p = 0.0087). A graded association was observed across M2 GEV quartiles without evidence of nonlinearity. Results remained directionally stable under winsorization, exclusion of distributional extremes, heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors, bootstrap resampling, leave-one-out analysis, repeated leave-five-out perturbations, and accounting for recording-center clustering. By contrast, M2 coverage, mean duration, and occurrence were not significantly associated with outcome after multiplicity correction. An outcome-blind decomposition of EEG after cardiac arrest identified a frozen microstate, M2, whose GEV was reproducibly associated with neurological outcome. The prognostic information associated with M2 was related primarily to the degree to which this spatial configuration explained the global EEG field rather than to its conventional temporal parameters. EEG microstate architecture may provide a complementary description of residual large-scale electrophysiological organization after hypoxic-ischemic brain injury. Rather than functioning as a standalone prognostic test, M2 GEV reflects residual spatial organization that complements established clinical and background EEG markers.

papers.title: Patient-Reported Outcomes with High-Volume Hemodiafiltration Versus High-Flux Hemodialysis Across Clinical Subgroups: Results from the CONVINCE Trial.
papers.abstract: High-volume hemodiafiltration (HDF) improves survival and attenuates decline in selected patient-reported outcome (PRO) domains versus high-flux hemodialysis (HD). Whether benefits differ across clinically relevant subgroups remains uncertain. We conducted a prespecified subgroup analysis of the multicenter CONVINCE randomized controlled trial comparing high-volume post-dilution HDF (≥23 L/session) with high-flux HD in adults receiving maintenance dialysis. Eight PROMIS domains were assessed quarterly over a median follow-up of 30 months. Linear mixed-effects models evaluated longitudinal PRO changes and treatment-by-subgroup interactions by prespecified baseline characteristics: age, sex, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, dialysis vintage, vascular access type, and residual urine volume. Joint-model sensitivity analyses of all eight longitudinal PROMIS trajectories and time to death assessed informative dropout due to death. Of 1360 randomized participants, 1211 with baseline and follow-up PRO assessments were included. PRO treatment effects were broadly consistent across prespecified clinical subgroups, without evidence of clinically meaningful heterogeneity. Models adjusted for baseline sociodemographic and clinical characteristics showed nominal treatment-by-subgroup interactions for dialysis vintage and physical function (P = 0.03), age and pain interference (P = 0.02), and dialysis vintage and sleep disturbance (P = 0.04). Joint-model sensitivity analyses accounting for informative dropout due to mortality reproduced the first two interactions and identified nominal interactions for vascular access type and sleep disturbance (P = 0.03) and cardiovascular disease status and cognitive function (P = 0.05). Interactions were modest in magnitude, exploratory, unadjusted for multiple comparisons, and not consistently observed across related PROMIS domains. This prespecified exploratory subgroup analysis found no convincing evidence of clinically meaningful treatment-effect heterogeneity across baseline characteristics examined. Nominal interactions were unadjusted for multiple comparisons and should be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Findings should not guide selection or exclusion of patients for high-volume HDF based on patient-reported outcomes.

papers.title: Measuring Sleep at Home in Adolescents With Autism Using EEG Headbands: Protocol for a Remote Study.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances are prevalent in autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) and worsen daytime functioning, yet their neural bases remain poorly understood. This may reflect the challenges of laboratory-based polysomnography for individuals with ASD, including sensory sensitivities and difficulty adapting to changes in routine. The advent of wearable electroencephalography (EEG) devices allows for remote data collection in the home and facilitates large-scale sleep studies. The aim of this study is to test the hypothesis that thalamocortical circuit dysfunction contributes to poor sleep in ASD by characterizing sleep oscillations that rely on this circuitry. To achieve this goal, we monitored sleep in the home using wearable EEG headbands in adolescents with ASD, including those who are profoundly affected, and their typically developing peers. When necessary, we used a desensitization protocol to gradually acclimate participants to wearing the headband overnight to promote the inclusion of individuals with sensory sensitivities and high support needs. Participants and their families completed assessments and questionnaires and received remote training to use a wearable EEG headband. Those needing time to acclimate followed a personalized 2-week desensitization protocol with a practice headband. Sleep was monitored at home for 3 consecutive nights, the first of which was for adaptation to the headband. Sleep data quality was checked daily, and remote technical support was provided as needed. Using sleep rhythms as physiological biomarkers of thalamocortical circuit function, we will test the hypothesis that abnormal circuit function in ASD is related to worse sleep quality. This study was funded by the Simons Foundation Autism Research Initiative (SFARI) and approved by the Mass General Brigham Institutional Review Board in November 2021. Data were collected between July 2023 and November 2025. A total of 146 participants (ASD: n=77; typically developing [TD]: n=65; profound autism: n=4) completed the study and produced at least 1 night of usable sleep data. Data analysis is underway, and the results will be submitted for publication in November 2026. At-home sleep monitoring enables large samples that are needed to characterize the neural underpinnings of sleep disturbances across the autism spectrum. The personalized desensitization protocol promotes inclusion by accommodating individuals often excluded from research due to sensory or behavioral challenges. These methods are adaptable for other conditions and research goals beyond ASD, such as longitudinal studies across development or characterizing sleep in other neurodevelopmental disorders. Desensitization protocols may also increase the tolerability of diagnostic laboratory-based sleep studies and other medical procedures, improving both patient experience and quality of care.

papers.title: The Mediating Role of Sleep Quality in Associations of Smartphone Addiction and Time-Specific Use With Prenatal Depression and Anxiety: Cross-Sectional Observational Study.
papers.abstract: Prenatal depression and anxiety have emerged as pressing global public health challenges. In the digital era, excessive smartphone use may exert complex effects on maternal mental health. Prior research has predominantly focused on adolescents, whereas evidence among pregnant women, particularly regarding total weekly use and use during critical circadian windows, such as after waking and before bedtime, remains limited. Furthermore, the mediating role of sleep quality in these associations has yet to be systematically examined. This study aimed to investigate the associations of smartphone addiction and time-specific smartphone use with prenatal depression and anxiety, and to assess the mediating role of sleep quality in these associations. This cross-sectional observational study enrolled 537 pregnant women. Smartphone use characteristics, sleep quality, and prenatal depression and anxiety were assessed using the Smartphone Addiction Scale-Short Version (SAS-SV), objective total weekly smartphone use recorded by the device, and self-reported duration of smartphone use after waking and duration of bedtime smartphone use; the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), and the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), respectively. Binary logistic regression was used to estimate associations, restricted cubic spline (RCS) models were used to explore nonlinear patterns, and exploratory mediation analyses were used to examine whether sleep quality statistically accounted for part of the observed associations. The prevalence of moderate-to-severe prenatal depression and anxiety was 8.8% (47/537) and 5.8% (31/537), respectively. After adjusting for covariates, smartphone addiction was associated with higher odds of depression (odds ratio [OR] 3.461, 95% CI 1.771-7.100) and anxiety (OR 7.738, 95% CI 3.064-23.172). Duration of smartphone use after waking ≥61 minutes and duration of bedtime smartphone use ≥91 minutes were also associated with higher odds of affective disorders. RCS analyses further revealed distinct nonlinear patterns across different exposure dimensions: duration of smartphone use after waking displayed U-shaped and J-shaped associations with depression and anxiety, respectively, while total weekly use displayed a U-shaped association with anxiety. Exploratory mediation analyses showed that the indirect pathways through sleep quality were statistically significant for the associations of bedtime smartphone use, weekly smartphone use, and smartphone addiction with prenatal depression, with mediation proportions of 44.89% (0.0065/0.0145), 31.30% (0.0056/0.0183), and 31.48% (0.0415/0.1315), respectively. The corresponding proportions in the anxiety models were 35.83% (0.0044/0.0123), 27.05% (0.0039/0.0144), and 22.73% (0.0271/0.1187). Smartphone addiction and excessive smartphone use after waking and before bedtime were associated with higher odds of prenatal depression and anxiety. Sleep quality may statistically account for part of these associations, but longitudinal studies are needed to establish temporal ordering and causal pathways.

papers.title: Comparison of Albino and Pigmented Rat Oxygen-Induced Retinopathy Models: From Vascular to Neural Retinal Changes.
papers.abstract: To compare two commonly used rat models of oxygen-induced retinopathy (OIR)-the 50/10 model in Sprague-Dawley rats and the 80/40 model in Long-Evans rats-to identify which more closely reproduces the features of human retinopathy. Dams and pups were exposed from postnatal day 0 (P0) to P14 to alternating oxygen cycles, followed by analyses at P14, P18, and P28. The 50/10 protocol alternated 50% and 10% oxygen every 24 hours, whereas the 80/40 protocol alternated 80% and 40% oxygen every 12 hours. The vascular, structural, and functional retinal changes were assessed using in vivo imaging and electrophysiology, as well as ex vivo histological and molecular analyses. Both OIR protocols induced significant retinal vascular abnormalities compared with controls, but with marked differences in onset, severity, and persistence. The 50/10 protocol produced earlier and more sustained vascular alterations, including reduced vascular coverage, increased vascular tortuosity, and neovascularization beginning at P14. Similar vascular changes appeared later and were less persistent in the 80/40 model. Retinal thinning occurred in both models; however, long-term photoreceptor segment thinning was observed only in the 50/10 protocol. The 50/10 protocol was associated with increased retinal cell death, significant cone photoreceptor loss, and mostly reduced electroretinographic responses, findings that were not observed in the 80/40 protocol. Both OIR models replicate features of human pathology, but differ in disease dynamics. These differences should be considered when selecting an OIR protocol, depending on whether vascular pathology or neurodegeneration is the primary therapeutic target.

papers.title: Sociodemographic and lifestyle correlates of accelerometer-measured 24-hour physical behavior patterns: a cross-sectional analysis of the ELSA-Brasil cohort.
papers.abstract: Physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep comprise an integrated 24-hour movement continuum that may influence health outcomes. While these behaviors have been studied separately, limited evidence exists on their combined patterns and related sociodemographic and lifestyle factors in middle-income countries like Brazil. The objective was to evaluate associations between sociodemographic and lifestyle correlates and accelerometer-measured 24-hour physical behavior patterns among Brazilian middle-aged and older adults. This cross-sectional analysis included 9,520 adults (mean age 59.2 ± 8.6 years) from the third wave of the ELSA-Brasil cohort study. Physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep were objectively measured using triaxial hip-worn accelerometers for seven consecutive days. Behavioral clusters were defined according to daily time spent in physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep using Partitioning Around Medoids cluster analysis. Sociodemographic and lifestyle factors were assessed via standardized questionnaires. Multinomial logistic regression models evaluated associations between correlates and behavioral clusters, with Cluster 3 as the reference category. Three clusters were identified: 1 (lower physical activity, higher sedentary behavior, shorter sleep), 2 (intermediate physical activity, intermediate sedentary behavior, intermediate sleep), and 3 (higher physical activity, lower sedentary behavior, longer sleep). Compared with Cluster 3, participants in Cluster 1 were more likely to be male, to have a higher body mass index, to have higher educational attainment, and to have a high income. Similar but weaker associations were observed for Cluster 2. Distinct 24-hour physical behavior patterns among Brazilian adults were associated with sociodemographic and lifestyle factors. These cross-sectional findings emphasize the need for targeted public health strategies promoting healthier 24-hour behavior profiles.
